title: NY State Senate · District 29
area: East Harlem in Manhattan and the South Bronx, including Mott Haven, Port Morris, and Melrose.

context.text: Uncontested general election: incumbent Jose M. Serrano (D, Working Families Party) defeated Nicholas Reyes 69.2%-30.0% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. No Republican or other-party candidate filed for the November 3 general election, so Serrano is unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Jose M. Serrano
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; unopposed in the general election
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 29 (since 2013); previously District 28 (2005-2013)

summary.text: Jose M. Serrano is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent running unopposed for re-election to NY Senate District 29, which covers East Harlem and the South Bronx. A lifelong South Bronx resident and the son of former U.S. Representative José E. Serrano, he served on the New York City Council before winning his Senate seat in 2004. He chairs the Senate Majority Conference and the Cultural Affairs, Tourism, Parks and Recreation Committee.

background.text: Born June 19, 1972, in New York City, and raised in the South Bronx; his father, José E. Serrano, served in the State Assembly and later the U.S. House of Representatives. His official biography describes him as a lifelong South Bronx resident.
Earned a B.A. in government from Manhattan College.
Before elected office, worked at the New York Shakespeare Festival, according to his official Senate biography, and served on Community Board 4.

Elected to the New York City Council in 2001 to represent District 17 in the Bronx, where his official biography says he chaired the Council's Committee on Cultural Affairs; he served until 2004 (Ballotpedia).

Elected to the State Senate in November 2004, defeating Republican incumbent Olga Mendez, who had switched parties earlier that year; he represented District 28 from 2005 to 2013 and has represented District 29 since 2013.
Chairs the Senate Majority (Democratic) Conference, a post Wikipedia dates to 2019, and chairs the Cultural Affairs, Tourism, Parks and Recreation Committee, which he also chaired in 2009-2010.
His committee assignments also include Aging, Environmental Conservation, Libraries, Social Services, Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs, and Women's Issues.

According to his official biography, as a committee chair during the 2010 budget negotiations he helped keep State Parks open, and he launched the Senate's "Open Legislation" tool for searching legislation; he also helped launch the "East Harlem Against Deportation" coalition.
According to his official biography, he lives in the South Bronx with his wife and their two children.

priorities.text: Healthcare access in the South Bronx, including securing funding for new medical infrastructure at local hospitals.
Environmental and climate legislation, reflected in a top-10% ranking on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 scorecard.
Cultural affairs, tourism, parks and recreation, as chair of the relevant Senate committee.

positions.summary: Scored 95 (top 10%) on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 legislative scorecard, which tracks votes on climate, clean water, and toxic-chemical bills.
positions.quote: He looks forward to continuing his environmental work with his colleagues in government and advocates to create a cleaner, healthier, and safer New York.

positions.summary: Helped secure roughly $1 million toward a new cardiac catheterization laboratory at Lincoln Hospital in the Bronx to address healthcare disparities for high-risk South Bronx patients.

record.text: Helped secure about $1 million toward a new cardiac catheterization laboratory at Lincoln Hospital in the Bronx, alongside other federal, state, and local officials and the Governor's office.
Scored 95 out of 100 (top 10% of legislators) on the Environmental Advocates New York 2026 legislative scorecard.

Chairs the Senate Cultural Affairs, Tourism, Parks and Recreation Committee in the 2025-2026 session; also sits on the Aging, Libraries, Women's Issues, Environmental Conservation, Social Services, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.

researchNotes: Serrano faces no opponent on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot; his Democratic primary opponent Nicholas Reyes is not included per the research standard. Serrano has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and has no separate campaign website distinct from his official Senate page, so priorities are drawn from official committee assignments and NYSenate.gov press coverage rather than campaign materials; positions beyond climate and healthcare could not be documented with a direct citable statement. Serrano's biographical details come from his official Senate biography, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia; no separate campaign biography was found.
